item.title: Texas Longhorns lose offensive tackle Trevor Goosby for rest of season
item.description: Texas Longhorns offensive lineman Trevor Goosby (74) leaves the field in a cart after going down with an injury in the first quarter of the Longhorns' game against the Mississippi Rebels at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Texas ' All-American offensive tackle Trevor Goosby suffered a knee injury and will be out for the rest of the season, ESPN reported Sunday. The 6-7, 325-pound senior, who has been projected as a first-round NFL Draft pick next spring, played only 14 snaps in Texas' win over Mississippi on Saturday before getting injured and carted off to the locker room. His 74.1 offensive PFF grade is the highest of any Texas offensive lineman. He did not allow a sack in 223 pass-blocking snaps and has given up just eight pressures and one quarterback hit. Senior Andre Cojoe replaced Goosby and graded out at a disappointing 57.4 rating, according to Pro Football Focus. He gave up one sack and another quarterback hurry. Wide receiver Cam Coleman suffered a shoulder injury and left the game and didn't return. There is no update on his condition. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Tom Brady rips officiating in Lions-Packers over soft calls
item.description: Credit: Fox Tom Brady got plenty of soft calls when he was under center for the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers during his playing days. Now that he’s in the booth though, he is getting pretty tired of them. During Sunday’s game between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, Brady was on the call alongside Kevin Burkhardt, and could not hold back his frustration after several penalties raised his ire. In the fourth quarter with the Lions holding a 17–14 lead, linebacker Derrick Barnes got called for unnecessary roughness on a late hit. “What?” Brady asked incredulously after seeing the flag. “There’s no way.” Watching the replay, Brady doubled down on his criticism of the flag, noting that the defender can’t assume that a pass is going to be dropped. “That’s allowed 99 out of 100. It’s a bang-bang play. I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you’re on the field you’ve got to pursue that ball. If he catches that, he needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball off him as a pass defense. He can’t go in there and put his hand on him.” Later in the quarter, another call got Brady especially riled up. With the game tied 17–17 and the Lions looking to drive for a game-winning field goal, quarterback Jared Goff stood tall in the pocket and took a big hit while delivering a ball to tight end Sam LaPorta for a healthy gain. The flag that Goff earned on the hit gave the Lions 15 yards on top of the play, and put them into field goal range. “No, my goodness. What is that?! RELATED: ENSHRINE FITZGERALD THEN LOSE The Cardinals have been a roller coaster this year. The new offense is going to take a while to get going, but there are glimmers of hope in every contest. Led all tacklers with seven. He is undoubtedly the best offensive player the Cardinals have. Proof of that is the hurdle in the fourth quarter. Led all receivers with 13 targets, 10 receptions for 11 yards and one score. K Chad Ryland – Another good day for Ryland who, once again, scored the majority of offensive points with nine as he connected on field goals of 30, 26, and 41 yards. After McBride, Ryland has been the offense MVP this year. How sad is that? Larry Legend forever stamped in AZ Cardinals history ❤️ pic.twitter.com/hUQha7MD5U — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 25, 2026 Larry Fitzgerald Enshrinement – First, the Hall of Fame, and now enshrined in Arizona Cardinals history forever. You gave your all, Larry. We still love you. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Lack of receiver play – Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are both exceptional receivers, yet Wilson only caught four balls all game. Bourne had six targets, but was only able to corral three catches for just nine yards. Jalen Brooks had one catch. These are all good pass catchers, and yet aren’t being utilized. No rushing attack – This is a huge breakdown for this offense. Yes, their best offensive lineman, Paris Johnson, is out for the year, but this group must be more consistent on running plays. Good teams run for more than 94 yards in a game. What was all that hype about when Tyler Allgeier was signed during the offseason? Eight rushes for 19 yards? Where were any Cardinals defenders when Nix left the pocket? It was like the entire field was wiped clean until he got inside the five-yard line. There weren’t any trailing defenders whatsoever. The Broncos ran up the gut way too many times and ended the contest with a 6.1 yards per carry average.

item.title: Raiders cannot complete mad dash as Rams push losing streak to four
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (2) is tackled in the second quarter of the game against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. LAS VEGAS—The Las Vegas Raiders gave themselves a puncher’s chance, but ultimately fell behind too far in the scorecards for it to matter. On Sunday, the Raiders dropped their fourth straight contest, falling to the Los Angeles Rams 35-21 at Allegiant Stadium. The main culprit was ultimately a slow start to the game, putting the Raiders as far back as 25 points before the second quarter was up. For much of the first half, the Raiders were struggling in virtually every aspect of play. The offensive line was being beaten practically every other snap as Kirk Cousins and the rest of the offense found it next to impossible to establish any sort of rhythm. It was the same case on defense, as the lack of sack production outside of Tonka Hemingway’s on the first Rams drive of the game allowed passing options to get open, while skill players were able to add yards after contact due to the struggles bringing ballcarriers down. “We have to go watch the film,” said Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak. “I think, at this point, we’re thinking about everything. How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter and personnel scheme. We got to talk about all of it.” The day was exemplified with the final scoring drive of the game, when the Raiders gave up three straight third-down conversions to set up a Blake Corum touchdown run that sealed their fate. There is a level of concern for the defense now, which is a shame given how improved it appeared to look over the first three games of the season. On top of giving up over 30 points for the fourth consecutive game, the Rams ran for 199 yards on the afternoon, only falling below 200 when Matthew Stafford took three knees in victory formation. Kyren Williams and Corum got a 50-50 split on the carries, rushing for 99 and 93 yards, respectively. Adding in Stafford’s three passing touchdowns in the first half to become the all-time Rams franchise leader in touchdowns, and that created a recipe for a day the Raiders would love to forget soon. “They’re moving the ball on us way too well. I got to go look at the tape,” said Kubiak on the Raiders run defense. The early lead forced the Raiders into a one-dimensional offensive script, abandoning a running game that once again struggled (Ashton Jeanty recorded only 15 rushing yards on eight carries). Cousins was forced to throw the football 44 times on the day, completing 26 of them for 295 yards and two touchdowns. The Raiders needing to air the ball out aided the final statlines of Jeanty (team-high eight receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown), Brock Bowers (six catches for 73 yards) and Tre Tucker (five catches for a game-high 103 yards and a touchdown), but the team made it abundantly clear that they would prefer not to have to resort to one plan of attack.

item.title: Raiders player of the game vs Rams is WR Tre Tucker
item.description: The Las Vegas Raiders suffered anothe disappointing loss to the Los Angeles Rams 35-21 on Sunday. The Raiders trailed 28-6 at halftime but came out energized in the second half. They cut the Rams' lead to 28-18 but couldn't get any closer. Las Vegas had a few solid players, with quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 295 yards and two touchdowns. Running back Ashton Jeanty caught six passes for 61 yards. On defense, Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean each added 12 tackles, but wide receiver Tre Tucker earned Player of the Game honors again. Raiders Week 7 Player of the Game -- WR Tre Tucker Tucker finished with five receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown; with 20.6 yards per catch, he was one of the few bright spots for the Raiders' struggling offense. Cousins faced constant pressure, the running game stalled, and Las Vegas couldn't finish drives. However, Tucker helped shift momentum in the fourth quarter with the explosive play the Raiders desperately needed. His 37-yard touchdown reception from Cousins gave the offense life and made the game interesting for a bit. The speedy receiver also caught a 41-yard reception, breaking through a few defenders to help set up a touchdown. In the future, the Raiders need more ways to get Tucker involved. His speed can stretch the defense and help tight end Brock Bowers on underneath throws. It also drags safety out of the box and opens up running lanes for the Raiders' running backs. Las Vegas needs to bring the five-year veteran into the game plan earlier, not wait until the fourth quarter. Waiting that long will help the offense be more consistent in the passing game. When he has the ball, he can make explosive plays, so it's time to incorporate him into the game plan more often. Tucker has 29 catches for a team-leading 474 yards and four touchdowns. After losing the 4th game in a row, Las Vegas has plenty of problems to address, like stopping the run and protecting the quarterback. Tucker's performance over the last two weeks could be something the offense builds around as they prepare for the rest of the season. item.title: Deshaun Watson’s Wife Sounds Off After Browns Down Titans
item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson keeps winning, with his latest victory coming against the Titans. Getty Deshaun Watson’s big day against the Tennessee Titans brought an emphatic response from his wife, Jilly Anais Watson. The Cleveland Browns improved to 5-2 with a 27-24 victory Sunday, and Anais wasted little time celebrating the quarterback’s latest win. “That boy 4 a bad MF! Another Sunday WIN baby. 4’s up,” she wrote on social media. She later posted a photo wearing Watson’s No. 4 Clemson jersey, adding another message for her husband. “A little obsessed with 4.” View this post on Instagram The posts continued a familiar theme for Anais, who has marked Cleveland’s victories throughout the season . This time, Watson gave her more than another late escape to celebrate. He topped 300 passing yards for the first time in a Browns uniform. item.title: Who Won the NASCAR Race at Talladega? Kyle Larson Pulls Off Stunning Last-Lap Victory
item.description: TALLADEGA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 25: Kyle Larson, driver of the #5 HendrickCars.com Chevrolet, takes the checkered flag to win the NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway on October 25, 2026 in Talladega, Alabama. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) Getty Kyle Larson looked like he had lost his chance to win at Talladega Superspeedway. Less than a lap later, he was celebrating one of the most improbable victories of the NASCAR Cup Series season. The Hendrick Motorsports driver went from the lead to roughly 11th on the final lap of Sunday’s YellaWood 500, only to charge back through traffic and take the checkered flag in a remarkable finish. And the championship implications were enormous. Larson entered Sunday’s race with a five-point lead over Christopher Bell. He left Talladega with an unofficial 73-point advantage over Denny Hamlin, putting himself in a commanding position with just two races remaining in NASCAR’s championship Chase. Stage 2: The ‘Big One’ Rocks NASCAR’s Championship Chase Talladega’s biggest wreck struck on Lap 132 , collecting 12 cars and dealing a devastating blow to several championship contenders. The accident began when Ryan Blaney lost momentum in the outside lane and Bubba Wallace couldn’t avoid hitting him from behind. Denny Hamlin , Tyler Reddick, Chase Elliott and several others were swept up in the pileup. Blaney was unable to continue, while Reddick and Elliott were among those sent to the garage. Championship leader Kyle Larson escaped the wreck and was scored as the leader under caution. Joey Logano ultimately won Stage 2 by just 0.012 seconds over Larson, who collected nine valuable stage points. Chase Briscoe finished third. Stage 1: RFK Racing Dominates as Christopher Bell Suffers Disaster RFK Racing turned Talladega’s early fuel-saving strategy into a major advantage. While most of the field slowed to conserve fuel, Chris Buescher, Ryan Preece and Brad Keselowski broke away, eventually building a lead of roughly 40 seconds. Buescher won the opening stage, followed by his two teammates. Larson finished fourth, earning seven stage points. But Christopher Bell, who entered Sunday just five points behind Larson, suffered a disastrous opening stage. Bell spun entering pit road on Lap 56 and hit the inside wall, triggering a series of tire problems, repairs and a pass-through penalty for too many crew members over the wall. item.title: Jonas Urbig: ‘Today we played for Vincent Kompany and Joshua Kimmich’
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - APRIL 15: Vincent Kompany, Head Coach of FC Bayern Munich, and Joshua Kimmich of FC Bayern Munich embrace after the team's victory in the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 Quarter-Final Second Leg match between FC Bayern München and Real Madrid CF at Football Arena Munich on April 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vincent Kompany’s collapse and Joshua Kimmich’s familial tragedy hit Bayern Munich hard during a difficult week of football. What is most important, of course, is that the duo and their families and friends recover and recuperate from these traumatic experiences. But it impacted Bayern’s players and staff, too. With a lot of players also succumbing to injuries, the team was either going to falter due to the adversity or use that adversity to give themselves motivation. The Bavarians’ mostly convincing 3-1 away victory against high-flying SC Freiburg demonstrated the team had done the latter, and starting goalkeeper Jonas Urbig confirmed as much in the post-match interview (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “Today we played for the coach and for Joshua Kimmich. I hope we made him [Kompany] proud, even though I prefer that he would rest.” Somehow, it is difficult to imagine Kompany refusing to watch the match, even in the hospital. Whether he has seen it already or will do so once he gets better, one can assume braving such adversity to demonstrate such a performance would be something for a coach to be quite proud of. item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Broncos’ Bo Nix joins extremely exclusive Lamar Jackson club in Cardinals Week 7 clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Broncos earned a big 30-16 Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. It was a bounce-back performance for quarterback Bo Nix , as he got it done through the air and with his legs. He played so well that Nix is now part of an exclusive quarterback club that includes Baltimore Ravens star Lamar Jackson . The 26-year-old became just the fourth quarterback in league history to record a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown that both went for 50+ yards in a single game , according to NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno. Nix joins Jackson, Justin Fields, and Cam Newton on the list. Jackson and Fields accomplished that feat in 2022, while Newton did it in 2012. Nix is the first individual to pull off a 50+ passing and rushing touchdown in the same game in the past five seasons. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bo Nix played a key part in leading the Broncos to their fifth win on the campaign. The former first-round pick ended the day with 222 passing yards, 74 rushing yards, and two total touchdowns (one passing, one rushing), while completing 51.7% of his pass attempts. He spread the ball around to nine different players, with seven of them reeling in at least one reception. The third-year veteran received plenty of flak for his play this season leading up to this contest. Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick lit up Bo Nix for his ugly performance in the Broncos’ 17-14 Week 6 win over the Seattle Seahawks in overtime. But Denver keeps winning, and the club sits near the top of the AFC West. Nix and the Broncos move on to Week 8, where they’ll take on the Kansas City Chiefs at home. On the Aggies’ first drive of the contest, Reed threw a pick-six, which jump-started what would become an impressive win for the Crimson Tide. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
